title: TTL enforcement for request/response logs store (batched purge + safety limits)
author: Logan Wright
release_notes: - Enforce tenant retention policies for request/response logs via background purge jobs with batching + throttling. - Adds operational guardrails (caps, backoff, kill-switch) to prevent DB pressure during large backlogs.
body:
## Context
We store request/response logs (aka request logs) for debugging, usage analysis, and customer support. As part of the Retention controls initiative, we need to enforce customer-configured TTLs in this store with predictable DB impact.

This PR wires TTL enforcement into the request logs store and adds a batched, rate-limited purge implementation built on the purge job framework introduced in pr-28489.

## What changed
- Adds a `request_logs_ttl_purger` job that deletes expired request/response logs based on the evaluated retention policy (effective TTL per tenant + region).
- Implements safe, batched deletion using an index-friendly query path to avoid long-running DELETEs and excessive lock contention.
- Introduces guardrails to cap work per run, and to throttle when DB load is elevated.
- Adds an operator-facing kill switch and dry-run mode.

## Purge algorithm (high level)
- Determine `cutoff_ts = now - effective_ttl` for each (tenant_id, region) partition.
- Select candidate row ids in small chunks using an index on `(tenant_id, region, created_at)`:
  - `SELECT id FROM request_logs WHERE tenant_id = ? AND region = ? AND created_at < ? ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT :batch_size`
- Delete by primary key to keep the delete statement bounded:
  - `DELETE FROM request_logs WHERE id = ANY(:ids)`
- Repeat until one of the safety limits is hit.

## Safety limits / DB pressure controls
Defaults are conservative and configurable via runtime config:
- `max_rows_per_run` (default: 250k)
- `max_batches_per_run` (default: 500)
- `batch_size` (default: 500)
- `max_runtime_per_run` (default: 10m)
- `inter_batch_sleep_ms` (default: 50ms)
- `db_cpu_soft_limit` (optional; when enabled, the job self-throttles using the existing DB load signal)

If the job hits a limit, it exits cleanly and will continue on the next scheduled run.

## Observability
- Emits per-run counters and timings:
  - `request_logs_purge_rows_deleted_total{tenant,region}`
  - `request_logs_purge_batches_total{tenant,region}`
  - `request_logs_purge_errors_total{tenant,region,reason}`
  - `request_logs_purge_run_duration_seconds`
- Logs structured events on start/stop with fields: tenant_id, region, cutoff_ts, rows_deleted, batches, exit_reason.

Note: standardized retention verification metrics (ttl lag, backlog sizing) are tracked separately (see ENG-18452 / pr-28540). This PR focuses on safe deletion mechanics for the request logs store.

## Files / areas touched (high level)
- `services/request-logs/ttl/purger.go`: store-specific purge logic + batching
- `services/request-logs/ttl/config.go`: runtime config + defaults + kill switch
- `services/request-logs/db/queries.sql`: new indexed select path (id-first)
- `services/control-plane/retention/client.go`: fetch effective TTL (uses cached evaluator)
- `cmd/worker/jobs/request_logs_ttl_purger.go`: job registration + schedule
- `docs/internal/runbooks/request-logs-ttl.md`: operator notes + debugging

## Testing
- Unit tests for:
  - batching loop exit conditions (row cap, runtime cap, batch cap)
  - retry/backoff behavior on transient DB errors
  - cutoff computation and tenant/region partitioning
- Integration test (nightly) using a seeded table with ~1M rows to validate:
  - deletes remain bounded (no single statement > batch_size)
  - job exits under `max_runtime_per_run`

Manual verification:
- Ran purge against staging with a simulated 30-day TTL and a synthetic backlog; confirmed steady delete rate and no elevated lock wait times.

## Rollout plan
- Ship behind `request_logs_ttl_enforcement_enabled` (default OFF).
- Enable in internal envs for 48h, then enable for design partners.
- Gradually increase `max_rows_per_run` once SRE signs off on DB load profile.

## Risks / mitigations
- Risk: backlog accumulation could cause long catch-up windows.
  - Mitigation: job is incremental; caps prevent DB overload; can temporarily raise caps during low-traffic windows.
- Risk: accidental over-deletion due to cutoff bugs.
  - Mitigation: uses server-side time; cutoff derived from effective TTL; includes dry-run mode and logs exit summaries.

## Checklist
- [x] Bounded deletes (batch size enforced)
- [x] Configurable safety caps
- [x] Idempotent / retryable behavior
- [x] Metrics + structured logs
- [x] Runbook stub added

## Commits
- feat(request-logs): add TTL purger job and config defaults
- refactor(db): implement id-first selection for safe batched deletes
- test(request-logs): add purge loop unit tests and integration fixture
- docs(runbooks): add request logs TTL operator notes

## Review notes
Allison Grant: Can we avoid emitting high-cardinality labels in metrics? tenant_id label will explode.
Logan Wright (author): Good catch. Removed `tenant_id` from Prometheus metric labels; kept tenant_id in structured logs only. Region label remains.

Sean Gallagher: Need a hard runtime cap + explicit exit reasons, otherwise on-call won’t know if we’re throttling vs erroring.
Logan Wright (author): Added `max_runtime_per_run` and `exit_reason` (row_cap|runtime_cap|batch_cap|no_work|error). Also added a log event at exit with summary.

Ethan Park: Make sure we’re using the control plane effective policy evaluation and not duplicating TTL rules here.
Logan Wright (author): Wired via `retention/client` (cached evaluator) and added a guard for tenants with request logging disabled.

Kevin Osei: Please align naming with retention policy data class `request_response_logs`.
Logan Wright (author): Updated config keys + comments to use `request_response_logs` terminology and added migration note in the doc.

## CI
- Initial run failed: `go test ./...` (flake in integration test timing)
- Re-run passed after increasing test timeout and removing a time-dependent assertion

## Merge
Merged via squash to `main`.
